title: Greedy CDCL without restarts versus resolution
formal: Is there a deterministic polynomial-time transformation which, given a CNF formula F and a resolution refutation \(\pi\) of F, outputs a legal greedy CDCL refutation of the same F, without restarts, in the asserting-learning model defined below? Both the transformation time and the output length are polynomial in the binary length of \((F,\pi )\).
definitions:
Literals are \(x_{i}\) or \(\neg x_{i}\) for \(i\in \{1,\ldots ,n\}\); clauses are sets of literals and F is a finite set of clauses. A resolution inference derives \((C\setminus \{x\})\cup (D\setminus \{\neg x\})\) from clauses C containing x and D containing \(\neg x\). A refutation is a finite sequence ending in the empty clause, each entry being an input clause or an inference from earlier entries, with parent indices and pivot recorded. Variable indices and pointers use binary notation. Clause and formula encodings explicitly list their literals.

A CDCL state consists of a database D containing F and an ordered trail of assignments to distinct variables of F. Each assignment is marked either as a decision or with its reason clause in D. Its decision level is the number of decisions up to that assignment. Initially \(D=F\) and the trail is empty. A clause is falsified if all its literals are false on the trail; it is unit if exactly one literal is unassigned and all others are false. The following priority of actions is mandatory.

If D has a falsified clause, a conflict must be processed before any other action. At decision level zero the run ends with UNSAT. Otherwise choose a falsified clause K and a trivial resolution analysis: start with K and repeatedly resolve the current clause with a reason clause recorded on the current trail, using a distinct pivot at each step. Every intermediate clause must be falsified by the current trail. Stop at a nonempty asserting clause C, meaning that exactly one of its variables has the current highest decision level. The trace records the full analysis. Add C to D and erase the suffix of the trail whose decision levels exceed a, where a is the maximum level of the other literals of C, or zero if there are none. Then perform one legal unit propagation and return to the conflict-first priority check.

If there is no conflict but a unit clause exists, choose such a clause, assign its unassigned literal to true, record that clause as the reason, and repeat the priority check. Only when neither conflicts nor units exist may a new decision assign either value to an unassigned variable. At such a stable state the run may first delete any subset of learned clauses, retaining all input clauses and all reasons appearing on the current trail, and must then make a decision. A satisfying complete trail ends with SAT, not a refutation. There is no independent operation clearing or shortening the trail: backjumping is allowed only after a conflict and only to the assertion level.

All choices of decisions, unit reasons, conflict clauses, trivial asserting analyses and permitted deletions are free components of the output trace. No fixed branching heuristic or first-UIP policy is imposed. No new variables, preprocessed replacement formula, unrecorded learned axioms or restarts are permitted. The only learned clauses are those derived by the recorded conflict analyses. The trace length counts all clauses, literals, assignments, analysis steps and pointers in an explicit binary encoding, so expensive analysis cannot be hidden in one step. This is the restart-free instantiation of the Vinyals model with arbitrary trivial asserting learning. The requested p-simulation is a uniform translation supplied with \(\pi\); mere existence of a short trace, or finding one from F alone, is a different claim.

context_blocks.text: Clause learning stores consequences of encountered conflicts and reuses them during a SAT search. General resolution permits arbitrary reuse of earlier clauses, without requiring that they arise along a current partial assignment. This question asks whether the constraints of a greedy search, even with freely chosen decisions and learning, impose a superpolynomial cost when restarting is unavailable.

The operational model matters. Exhaustive unit propagation and immediate conflict processing constrain which trails are reachable. A restart discards the current trail while retaining learned information, whereas a backjump must be justified by the newly learned asserting clause. The statement specifies those actions separately rather than treating every return to decision level zero as a prohibited restart.

Vinyals gives an execution-trace proof system with explicit propagation reasons, conflict-analysis derivations, deletion rules and cost measures. The present card selects its no-restart policy and allows arbitrary trivial asserting analyses. This avoids making the question depend on a particular solver implementation, while retaining actual greedy search restrictions.

The supplied resolution proof is part of the translator’s input. An affirmative answer therefore would not give a polynomial-time SAT solver or a practical heuristic that discovers short proofs unaided. A theorem guaranteeing only polynomial-size traces, without a polynomial-time translation, would establish the corresponding size-simulation statement rather than the full p-simulation asked here.

Vinyals’ 2022 exposition distinguishes known simulations using non-greedy propagation or preprocessing from the unresolved greedy no-restart comparison. Buss and Thapen’s later work identifies candidate formulas for separating related resolution systems but does not prove that separation. These results motivate the target without establishing a resolution of the operational model on this card.

why: Determine whether eliminating restarts changes the proof-generating power of greedy clause-learning search by more than a polynomial factor.
answer_criterion: Prove the proposition in the problem statement or its logical negation, with the stated model, domains, promises and quantifiers. A conditional theorem settles only its conditional version. Benchmark acceptance requires a complete proof-assistant-verified proof matching the full target.

importance.reason: A concrete bridge between SAT solving and proof complexity: it isolates the computational role of restarts while allowing helpful search choices. The significance comes from the unresolved comparison with general resolution and explicit specialist discussion, not from an unspecified explanation of solver performance.

progress.text: The Vinyals thesis specifies a greedy operational CDCL proof system with explicit conflict analysis, deletion and restart policies.
The specialist exposition distinguishes the no-restart question from known non-greedy and preprocessing simulations.
Buss–Thapen discuss candidates for separating pool resolution from resolution without establishing such a separation. This is related evidence, not an equivalence claim for every CDCL model.

status_note: Checked through 11 September 2026. No p-simulation or separation for the specified greedy operational model was found. Known non-greedy or preprocessing simulations do not meet its restrictions. The cited pool-resolution discussion does not by itself identify pool resolution with this particular trace system.
review_note: Explicit model choice: Vinyals 2017, Paper D, with no restarts, arbitrary decisions and propagation order, trivial asserting clause learning, and optional permitted deletion. All transitions and encoding costs are written out. Neither first-UIP-only learning nor an asserted equivalence with pool resolution is substituted for the approved question.

statement_review.reason: The target and computational model are explicitly specified. This is an editorial review, not a formal verification of the statement or cited proofs.
